item.title: Race as a construct: busting medical myths with Dr. Joel Bervell
item.description:
Dr. Joel Bervell is an award winning trailblazer in clinical science communication. In addition to his practice he has built a science communication channel focusing on racial disparities in clinical care. Here he analyses two twins that could be considered different races despite being siblings from the same parents.
Responding to race as a social construct. Social construct does not mean imaginary. Race impacts are very real. When we think of skincare, hair care, economic conditions, treatment by police, we see clear delineations of racial impacts.
The history of the construction of race is wild to dive into. Standard repost disclosures: I am NOT Joel Bervell, he is found on yt, ig, tt, @joelbervell to follow, support, and engage with

item.description: MapQuest’s mobile app has consequently surged in popularity, rising its way to becoming the number one navigation app in all of the US on Apple’s App Store. It’s become so popular, in fact, that it also climbed to the fourth position on the App Store’s Top Charts, which excludes games, and number eight overall across apps and games. "We’re not changing it,” MapQuest declared in the viral post with a screenshot of a map showing Lake Ontario. item.title: Victory!!
item.description: In 2020, just 5 months after my father passed away, I was diagnosed with breast cancer. I didn’t know if I had enough strength to fight this battle, but with the loving support of my family and friends, I got through it, and today I got to the milestone of being 5yrs cancer free! I am so thankful to everyone who helped me, including the doctors and nurses, so, thank you to all of them! Also, thanks to all of you here on imjur, who sent me well wishes & encouragement at the beginning of this journey! To those of you out there who are still battling any kind of cancer, you are in my thoughts, and I wish you a full & speedy recovery. Never underestimate your ability to fight this battle. You are stronger than you think!

item.description:
The boys still do not recognize this as a bed they can get inside. It's just for sitting on. And they are always right.
Little Bear, big bed :D
Beginning of the laze...
Social laziness
Sun baths
Sleepy Salerno
Salerno sandwich lol
Monday morning cuddles(bear censoring a nipple)
Bob alert!
Found a different lantana bush on my skate today, on a road I haven't skated in a while. I think I remember it, I don't think it's a new discovery. But it's got gorgeous flowers
Roses are not my favorite, not even close, and yet we have some lovely rose bushes dotted around town. Fun longboarding sidenote I want to share with y'all: so when I started my skate today I immediately realized something was wrong with my board. Super wobbly. I could not control the board over 20mph. I thought the trucks had loosened up but when I flipped it over I found that one of my pivot cups in one of the trucks had deteriorated and most of it fell out. So I skated to my favorite local boardshop: NC Boardshop. The staff are awesome and have helped me with donations to a non-profit that I worked with in the past. They didn't have the right size, but they gave me one that was pretty close. They even called some of the skate shops in Santa Cruz to see if they carried the right size, but no luck. So we put a smaller pivot cup in. "MacGuyver'd" we said. And it worked fantastically!!! I was afraid I was gonna have to head home early but because of their efforts I hit all my favorite spots and skated for another 4 hours!!! I called them twice that afternoon to say thanks; once when I skated down the hill in front of their shop to let them know it seemed to be working, and at the end of my session to let them know they totally saved my day. TLDR: local skate shop rescued my day, and my health and safety :)
